title: fix(core): improve windows sandbox reliability and fix integration tests

triage_metadata.reasoning: No source files were pruned; all PR modifications directly address the reported issue.

summary.problem: Sandboxed process execution pathways suffer from resource leaks and uncleaned temporary sandbox artifacts when execution completes, fails, or is aborted early.
summary.root_cause: Execution paths in `SandboxedFileSystemService`, `ShellExecutionService`, `GrepTool`, `ToolRegistry`, and `shell-utils` omitted cleanup calls or relied on standard event listeners that did not fire during synchronous exceptions or generator cancellations.
summary.context: Identified during Windows sandboxing review (#24480), sandbox preparation produces temporary resources (such as manifests and sidecar processes) whose `prepared.cleanup()` callback must be guaranteed execution via `try...finally` blocks.

steps: In `SandboxedFileSystemService` (`packages/core/src/services/sandboxedFileSystemService.ts`), wrap process spawning and event handling in `readFile` and `writeTextFile` with `try...finally` blocks that execute `prepared.cleanup?.()` in `finally`.

In `ShellExecutionService` (`packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts`), capture `prepared.cleanup` as `cmdCleanup` in `childProcessFallback` and `executeWithPty`, ensuring `cmdCleanup?.()` is invoked in `catch` blocks when process execution fails.

In `GrepToolInvocation` (`packages/core/src/tools/grep.ts`), store the sandbox preparation `cleanup` callback and wrap the process `spawn` execution inside a `try...finally` block that invokes `cleanup?.()`.

In `ToolRegistry` (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.ts`), capture `prepared.cleanup` as `cleanupFunc` in `DiscoveredToolInvocation.execute` and `ToolRegistry.discoverTools`, placing `spawn` execution within `try...finally` blocks to guarantee `cleanupFunc?.()` is run.

In `shell-utils` (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`), update `spawnAsync` and `execStreaming` to wrap `spawn` execution and line iteration in `try...finally` blocks that trigger `prepared.cleanup?.()`.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: All sandbox process execution paths across file system operations, shell executions, grep tools, and tool discovery reliably execute cleanup callbacks (`prepared.cleanup()`) upon completion, failure, or early cancellation.
verification_steps: Run sandbox and shell execution core test suite: `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts src/services/sandboxedFileSystemService.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts`.
Verify that temporary sandbox artifacts and sidecar processes are cleaned up without resource leaks in both success and error scenarios.
